hypothesis: The parent action's local frame is Lorentzian, so the boost of wave O7 fixes the Robertson-Mansouri-Sexl parameters alpha = -1/2, beta = 1/2, delta = 0 (wave O8, uet_rms_light_speed.py, derived from exact light-travel times, with Galilean and contraction-only controls). Then the two-way speed of light depends neither on orientation (P_MM = beta - delta - 1/2 = 0, Michelson-Morley) nor on the laboratory velocity (P_KT = alpha - beta + 1 = 0, Kennedy-Thorndike). With T013 (time dilation, Ives-Stilwell) this covers all three parameters of the Lorentz transformation.

observable.quantity: P_MM and P_KT (each zero for the Lorentz transformation in every sign convention)
observable.domain: laboratory moving at about 370 km/s relative to the CMB frame (v/c ~ 1.2e-3); rotating optical cavities (Herrmann et al. 2009) and a cryogenic sapphire oscillator against hydrogen masers over six years (Tobar et al. 2010)

prediction_method.description: Model P_MM and P_KT from the boost, computed in 60-digit arithmetic (both zero to better than 1e-20); measured P_MM = (4 +- 8)e-12 and P_KT = (-4.8 +- 3.7)e-8 (weighted mean of the sidereal and annual terms) from the registered file; z = |measured - model| / sigma for each.

fixed_parameters: registered values and 1-sigma uncertainties exactly as in RMS_MM_KT_2009_2010
P_KT is the published weighted mean, not the sidereal or annual term alone
sign conventions of the papers are not converted; only |measured - 0| enters z
fail_criterion: FAILED if z_MM > 3 or z_KT > 3; INCONCLUSIVE otherwise.
note: Disclosure: drafted after reading both published values, so the outcome is effectively known (|P_MM|/sigma = 0.5, |P_KT|/sigma = 1.3); the producer was not run before approval. Choice of experiments is the AI's: Herrmann et al. 2009 is the most precise rotating-cavity P_MM found; Tobar et al. 2010 the most precise P_KT found; neither was checked against the printed journal page. Scope: tests the Lorentz transformation of the parent action's local frame for light in electromagnetic resonators; any Lorentz-invariant theory passes, so this is not UET-distinct. The contraction-only control (Lorentz-FitzGerald without time dilation) passes Michelson-Morley and fails Kennedy-Thorndike, which is why both are required. Physics tests: core/05_tests/physics/test_rms_light_speed.py. Approved by the author on 2026-11-18 as drafted. Amendment 1, approved by the author on 2026-11-18 after the first run: that run (commit 932f999cb) gave FAILED (z_MM = 16.5) because the script computed the model P_MM in 64-bit floats at v = 1e-3 and got -1.3e-10 from rounding instead of 0. The model computation now uses 60-digit arithmetic and a physics test requires the model error to be below 1e-20. Data, observable, pass and fail rules are unchanged. The first run stays in core/UPDATE_LOG.md and the work ledger.
